newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE/CBOT T-bond link gets off to moderate start.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE/CBOT T-bond link gets off to moderate start.

text.p: U.S. Treasury futures enjoyed reasonable volume at the open of the new LIFFE/CBOT link in London on Friday, dealers said.
The link enables traders to use open outcry to trade the Bund and T-bond futures on both the Chicago Board of Trade and the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE).
Some 1,200 contracts had been traded by 0730 GMT after trade initially kicked off in the gilt pit to allow room for the opening flurry.
But traders said the link faced strong competition from Project A, the Chicago Board of Trade after-hours electronic trading system, which may drain volume from the new T-bond contract on LIFFE.

"To compete with Project A, we need to see 5,000 contracts daily, just to prove there's a need," said a local trader on LIFFE. "But really 10,000 would be ideal to ensure that this contract, unlike the last one, will survive."
LIFFE's last foray into T-bonds ended in 1993 when T-bond futures and options were suspended after volume dived.

Speaking at a press conference to launch the link, LIFFE chairman Jack Wigglesworth said the strategy would further cement LIFFE's position as Europe's leading exchange, both pre and post European Economic and Monetary Union.
Trading on Friday was brisk, but some dealers said they were concerned the volume was not as strong as they had expected.
By 0745 GMT, the June T-bond futures contract had reached a high of 110-09 and an early low of 110-04.
